newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-GRAF UNDERGOES KNEE SURGERY, TO MISS WIMBLEDON.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF UNDERGOES KNEE SURGERY, TO MISS WIMBLEDON.

text.p: Steffi Graf will miss Wimbledon and possibly the U.S. Open championships after undergoing a knee operation in Vienna on Tuesday, Austrian television said.
Graf, who was knocked out of the French Open in the quarter-finals last week, had the operation in a private hospital.
The seven times Wimbledon champion was reportedly recovering in a clinic and would be out of action for four months.
The report could not be immediately confirmed.
Graf has been suffering from a damaged tendon, but there were no indications before Tuesday that she was about to have surgery.
The German was sidelined for three months earlier this year with another knee injury and was a fourth round casualty at the Australian Open complaining afterwards of an infected toe.
Graf, the defending Wimbledon champion, slipped to number three in the world rankings following her shock loss to South Africa's Amanda Coetzer in Paris.
The report on ORF television said the operation was necessary because the knee cap was hanging too low, causing chronic irritation to the tendons in the patella.
Earlier on Tuesday, the German news agency SID reported that Graf would "in all probability" play in a WTA tournament in Eastbourne, England next week.
Wimbledon starts on June 23 and the U.S. Open begins on August 25.
